diagnostics.note: Diagnostics, reported apart from the benchmark: never in its values, comparisons, agreement figures or audit samples. The regression diagnostics follow the comparison rules frozen with them; the mapping diagnostic is labelled and forced (each case-level run's first cases-channel-only cases mapped and packed by the production code).

regression.question: Which weight-shift-control aircraft accidents have a probable cause that cites the pilot's decision making?
regression.origin: Task 10e kept this question as a regression case (REGRESSION_CASES, evals/retrieval/adoption/validate.ts): on Track C's coded labels its nDCG@6 fell from 65.8% under retrieval.v1 to 25.9% under retrieval.v2 and retrieval.v2-nf, in every scope sample (the task 10e report, section 5).

comparison.rule: For each variant against the base: the difference of the means over the scope samples, with bounds over the unknown labels as the benchmark computes them (cross-endpoint for nDCG@6, joint over shared unknowns for P@6 and supported P@6), and the same per sample. The conclusion rests on the primary metric's mean difference: 'regression' when its upper bound is below zero, 'no-regression' when its lower bound is at or above zero, 'inconclusive' otherwise. The other metrics are reported and never change it. The cases each variant's bundle displaced from the base's, and admitted, are listed per sample with their labels and coded status. The result is reported apart from the benchmark: never in its aggregates, comparisons, agreement figures or audit samples.

reproduction.source: The task 10e report, section 5: the coded nDCG@6 of every scope sample, to 0.1 point.

regression.scope: Phase A's cached development scope samples of this question (task 10d), the input task 10e measured the regression with; the three samples are identical.

mapping.note: Labelled diagnostic, forced: each case-level run's first cases that only the cases channel returned were mapped (`mapCasesToPassages`) and packed (`fetchAndPack`) by the production code as leading candidates. It measures what the mapping delivers for real questions, not how often production maps. Model-judged; reported apart from the benchmark.

agreement.note: Diagnostics, not validation: agreement between model judges (and with the adjudicator) measures their consistency, not their correctness; kappa 0.7 and agreement 0.8 are investigation thresholds.
